body.x: KOMATECH (CEO Han-Young Jung, www.myfreedy.com) introduced two of its Freedy wireless charging pad devices at CES 2015, which will run Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

The Freedy Dual Wireless Charger is capable of charging two smart devices wirelessly at the same time and can charge up to three devices in both wired and wireless mode by using the USB port on its lateral side. In accordance to the Qi Standard of the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC), the Freedy Dual Wireless Charger can wirelessly charge any smart device in the world supporting the Qi Standard. The device comes with a temperature sensing gauge and an overcurrent protection graft to help ensure the safety of its users. An average full charge under the device, using its 2,200 mAh battery, will take less than 4 hours. With its Qi standard certification, a wide variety of mobile devices can freely charge, in any part of the world, using this device.

The Freedy Hybrid Wireless Charger can be used in either a stand or pad format according to the user’s preference. It provides convenience for users by allowing them to watch a video or carry out a number of basic tasks on the user’s smart phone while being charged. It also comes fitted with a micro USB input so that charging can be done by connecting to a laptop or PC.

A spokesperson for KOMATECH shared, “Through the upcoming CES we plan to vigorously promote our 'Freedy' brand to the markets of Europe and the Americas while expanding our overseas markets through a series of positive meetings with global buyers.”

KOMATECH was formed in 1995, with a focus on the development of a variety of mobile device antennas. Utilizing existing charging technology and developing wireless ones, the company is a pioneer in its field.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
